question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-4,0],$ compute $P(X<-\sqrt{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-4,0],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4},\, & -4\le x\le 0, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<-\sqrt{2}) & =P(-4\le X<-\sqrt{2}) \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{-\sqrt{2}}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{-\sqrt{2}}\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{-\sqrt{2}-(-4)}{4} \\  & =1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
